title: C-circle assay for detection of alternative lengthening of telomere activity in FFPE tissue
author: Idilli, Segura-Bayona, et al.
materials: Cellular pellets should be harvested without enzymatic treatment. The protocol is suitable when starting with 7.0 ×106 – 1.0 ×108 cells.Note: FFPE-block preparation can be done up to 1 month in advance, but we recommend using freshly cut sections of FFPE samples as starting material for DNA extraction.Note: Care should be taken in the handling of chemicals and, if possible, they should be weighed/poured in a fume hood. Containers should have close-fitting lids.Note: Medium for tissue culture should be pre-warmed at 37°C.4.Harvesting the cellsa.Subculture cells 1–2 days before harvesting to achieve confluence in a 150 mm tissue-culture (TC) treated dish.b.Gently rinse cell monolayer with 25 mL of pre-warmed serum-free TC media (rock gently, remove and discard).c.Add 10 mL of warm serum-free TC media.d.Dislodge cells using a sterile cell scraper (“rubber policeman”).e.Transfer cells into a sterile, 15 mL conical centrifuge tube.f.Gently pellet cells from the media (centrifuge at 1000× g) for 5 min.5.Fixing the cellsNote: Use a fixation time of 16–24 h, longer fixation times can lead to severe DNA fragmentation, resulting in poor performance of the assay.a.Remove the supernatant from the tube leaving approximately 1 mL behind.b.Resuspend the cells by flicking the tube.c.Transfer suspended cells into a clean 1.5 mL microtube.d.Pellet the cells (centrifuge at 8000× g) for 30 s in a microcentrifuge. Discard the supernatant, leaving approximately 100–200 μL behind.e.Loosen pellet by gently flicking the tube and fix adding 1 mL of 10% neutral buffered formalin. Incubate pellet in fixative solution at 20°C–23°C for a minimum of 16 h, up to a maximum of 24 h.6.Removing the fixativea.Pellet the cells (centrifuge at 8000× g) for 30 s in the microcentrifuge. Carefully discard the supernatant by pipetting if necessary, to remove all the fixative. Avoid sucking up the cells.b.Loosen pellet by gently flicking the tube and add 1 mL of PBS.c.Pellet the cells (centrifuge at 8000× g) for 30 s in the microcentrifuge. Carefully discard the supernatant, by pipetting if necessary, to remove all the PBS. Avoid sucking up the cells.7.Creating the agarose pelletNote: Follow safety procedures and use thermo-protective gloves when removing agarose from the microwave.Note: The agarose gel needs to surround the pellet, but it is ideal to try to keep the cells as a pellet rather than mixing them up too much.a.Prepare the agarose gel (with an appropriate percentage of 1.5%–2%) by combining 0.75 g of agarose and enough ddH2O to reach a volume of 50 mL. Heat the solution in a microwave and create the gel (typically will take about 2 min).b.Leave the agarose gel to cool down for a few minutes at 20°C–23°C. The gel should have cooled substantially and reached a temperature that is safe to handle.c.Loosen pellet by gently flicking the tube and pipette 200–500 μL of agarose gel to pellet-containing microtube. Gently mix agarose with cells.d.Allow the agarose to set and then add 200 μL 70% EtOH to prevent the agarose drying out. Process the agarose pellets to embedding.8.Sample embeddingNote: Thoroughly dehydrate samples prior to embedding to remove residual formalin that could inhibit the subsequent proteinase K digestion during DNA isolation.a.Process the agarose pellets using a Tissue-Tek VIP® 6 AI and embed in CellWax Plus (CellPath GCA 030200A) according to manufacturer instructions.

A protocol modification of Qiagen QIAamp® DNA FFPE Tissue Kit is used to isolate genomic DNA from FFPE sections (https://www.qiagen.com/us/resources/resourcedetail?id=67ecad65-5f6c-4559-ae24-b614180bfc4b&lang=en). This method provides a reproducible and consistent genomic DNA yield.Note: As starting material, we recommend using freshly cut FFPE sections with a minimum of paraffin around the samples. We recommend starting with 3-8 sections per sample, each with a thickness of 5 μm. As a maximum limit for one preparation do not exceed 8 sections with a thickness of 10 μm each and a surface area of 250 mm2 (Figure 2).

According to the instrument used for chemiluminescence detection, quantitation and analysis of the slot-blot should be performed with an image processing software such as Image Lab™ Software (BioRad) (https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/10000076953.pdf) or ImageJ (https://imagej.net/Fiji/Downloads), where the original file format can be used to quantify the mean value intensity of each dot.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and safety
steps.instruction: Prepare all working buffers in advance (store up to 6 months at 20‑23 °C or –20 °C). Verify sufficient Phi29 DNA polymerase (store ≤24 months at –20 °C) and DTT (keep at –20 °C, avoid repeated freeze‑thaw). Wear gloves and lab coat, use sterile DNase/RNase‑free consumables.

steps.title: Harvest adherent cells for FFPE
steps.instruction: Grow U2OS or HeLa cells to confluence in a 150 mm tissue‑culture dish (subculture 1–2 days before).

substeps.instruction: Rinse monolayer with 25 mL pre‑warmed serum‑free media, discard.
Add 10 mL warm serum‑free media.
Dislodge cells with a sterile cell scraper.
Transfer suspension to a sterile 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 5 min; keep 7.0 × 10⁶ – 1.0 × 10⁸ cells.

steps.title: Fix cells in formalin
steps.instruction: Fix harvested cells for 16–24 h at 20‑23 °C.

substeps.instruction: Remove supernatant, leaving ~1 mL.
Resuspend cells by flicking the tube.
Transfer suspension to a clean 1.5 mL microtube.
Centrifuge at 8,000 × g for 30 s; discard supernatant, leaving 100–200 µL.
Add 1 mL 10 % neutral‑buffered formalin, incubate 16–24 h at 20‑23 °C.

steps.title: Remove fixative and wash
steps.instruction: Wash fixed cell pellets to eliminate formalin.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 8,000 × g for 30 s; carefully pipette off all supernatant.
Add 1 mL PBS, flick to loosen pellet.
Centrifuge at 8,000 × g for 30 s; remove PBS completely.

steps.title: Embed cells in low‑melt agarose
steps.instruction: Surround cell pellet with 1.5‑2 % agarose and prevent drying.

substeps.instruction: Prepare agarose: dissolve 0.75 g agarose in ddH₂O to 50 mL (≈1.5 % w/v); microwave ~2 min.
Cool agarose at 20‑23 °C for a few minutes until safe to handle.
Pipette 200–500 µL cooled agarose into the cell pellet tube, mix gently.
Allow agarose to solidify, then add 200 µL 70 % ethanol to prevent drying.

steps.title: Paraffin embed agarose pellets
steps.instruction: Dehydrate agarose pellets and embed in CellWax Plus using a Tissue‑Tek VIP® 6 AI according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Select and section FFPE tissue blocks
steps.instruction: Prepare 5 µm sections from qualified FFPE blocks.

substeps.instruction: Have a pathologist verify block quality; select blocks with ≥2 mm² tissue surface and no damage.
If block surface was exposed to air, discard the first 2–3 sections.
Collect 3–8 sections per sample (tumor or normal) into 1.5 mL microtubes; aim for at least three replicate tubes per condition.
Store tubes at +4 °C for up to 10 days (use sections within 10 days of cutting).

steps.title: Deparaffinize sections
steps.instruction: Remove paraffin and residual xylene from FFPE sections.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑heat two thermomixers to 37 °C and 56 °C.
Reconstitute Buffer AW1: add 25 mL 96‑100 % ethanol to 19 mL AW1 concentrate.
Reconstitute Buffer AW2: add 30 mL 96‑100 % ethanol to 13 mL AW2 concentrate; shake and equilibrate 15 min at 20‑23 °C.
Add 1 mL xylene to each 1.5 mL tube containing the sections, vortex 30 s.
Centrifuge at 20,000 × g (≈14,000 rpm) for 2.5 min at 20‑23 °C; remove supernatant.
Add 1 mL 96‑100 % ethanol, vortex 30 s.
Centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 3 min at 20‑23 °C; discard supernatant.
Air‑dry residual ethanol at 20‑23 °C (or up to 37 °C) for ~10 min; do not overdry.
Pre‑heat thermomixer to 90 °C for the next step.
Resuspend pellet in 180 µL Buffer ATL, add 20 µL proteinase K, vortex.
Incubate at 56 °C, 1400 rpm, for 1 h until fully lysed.

steps.title: Reverse formalin cross‑links
steps.instruction: Incubate lysate at 90 °C for 1 h to improve DNA yield.

substeps.instruction: Briefly spin tube, let sample cool 1–2 min to 20‑23 °C.
Add 2 µL RNase A (100 mg/mL) and incubate 2 min at 20‑23 °C.
For each sample, mix N × 200 µL Buffer AL with N × 200 µL 96‑100 % ethanol (N = number of samples).
Add 400 µL Buffer AL/ethanol mixture to the lysate, vortex (white precipitate may appear).
Spin briefly, transfer entire lysate to a QIAamp MinElute column in a 2 mL collection tube.
Centrifuge at 6,000 × g (8,000 rpm) for 1 min; discard flow‑through.
Add 500 µL Buffer AW1 (do not wet column rim), centrifuge 6,000 × g for 1 min.
Add 500 µL Buffer AW2, centrifuge 6,000 × g for 1 min.
Dry membrane by centrifuging at 20,000 × g (14,000 rpm) for 3 min.
Place column in a clean 1.5 mL tube; add 23 µL 10 mM Tris, pH 7.6 (equilibrated 20‑23 °C) to the membrane centre.
Incubate 5 min at 20‑23 °C.
Centrifuge at 20,000 × g (14,000 rpm) for 1 min; collect eluate.
Repeat the addition of 23 µL Tris to the same column, incubate 5 min, centrifuge again; combine eluates.
Keep DNA on ice until quantification.

steps.title: Analyze slot‑blot images
steps.instruction: Quantify C‑circle signals using image‑analysis software and normalize to controls.

substeps.instruction: Open chemiluminescence images in Image Lab or ImageJ.
Measure mean intensity of each dot on the telomere‑probed membrane.
Subtract global background (DNA‑omitted lane) from each sample value.
Subtract specific background (no Phi29 polymerase) from the Phi29‑treated values.
Normalize to loading control by dividing telomere intensity by the corresponding Alu‑repeat intensity (after background subtraction).
If comparing multiple blots, express each sample as a fraction of the U2OS positive‑control signal.
Plot C‑circle activity (CCA) as histograms; interpret ALT status using the described fold‑change thresholds (≤2‑fold = ALT‑negative, ≥5‑fold = ALT‑positive, etc.).
